title: Same eyes, more worldly upbringing, actually trained: each member's EfficientNet-B0 trunk starts from Noisy Student weights instead of plain ImageNet weights (re-run of experiment 24, which never reached a GPU)
init_strategy: pretrained:tf_efficientnet_b0.ns_jft_in1k (Noisy Student, Apache-2.0, ported into torchvision's EfficientNet-B0 layout with TF-same padding)
hypothesis: Experiment 24's hypothesis was never tested. Its run died before training: AWS had no g6.xlarge capacity in any eu-central-1 zone (spot or on-demand; train_berlin.log ends 'no capacity for g6.xlarge anywhere in the region'), so the scorer recorded 1e9 and the harness marked it REVERTED. That verdict says nothing about Noisy Student weights, just as experiment 17's crash said nothing about ring pooling (re-run as 18). The same is true of experiment 21 (LP-FT, AWS endpoint connection error). The reasoning stands unchanged on the current champion (exp 20, mission 0.0777: usable 93.0%, false 0.75%, abstain 6.25% on held-out truedop_2024; the three training photographs at 100% usable at the same viewpoints). Every large step on the never-seen photograph in this era came from what the trunk brought with it: from-scratch -> MobileNetV3-Small 10.75% -> 49.5% usable (exp 12), MobileNetV2 86.75% (exp 16), EfficientNet-B0 92.5% (exp 19). Since then, changes to the training procedure have given at most half a point (exp 20 weight averaging, kept) or lost ground (exp 22 continuous vantages 0.103, exp 23 cross-survey JS consistency 0.090). Bigger trunks are ruled out by the size gate (two B0 members = 31.7 MB of 33.6 MB), so this changes the trunk's KNOWLEDGE and keeps its SIZE: same EfficientNet-B0, initialised from the Noisy Student checkpoint (Xie et al. 2020; ImageNet + 300M pseudo-labelled JFT images under RandAugment, dropout and stochastic depth). Its headline result is out-of-distribution robustness (ImageNet-C/-P/-A: blur, noise, brightness, contrast, weather), and that is the photometric half of a survey change. No experiment in any era has varied the pretraining SOURCE of a fixed architecture. Builds on experiment 20 (champion) and is otherwise identical to experiment 24's pre-registered design, whose code survives in runs/20261102_104104_experiment24/model_src/.
method: ONE change, identical to experiment 24: the file each member's trunk is initialised from goes from torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1 (model/pretrained/effb0_features7.pt) to timm's tf_efficientnet_b0.ns_jft_in1k, ported into torchvision's features[0..7] layout (model/pretrained/effb0ns_features7.pt, already baked and numerically checked by experiment 24's port script model/pretrained/port_effb0_ns.py; both files are still on disk). The TF checkpoint was trained with 'SAME' padding, so the five stride-2 convs (the stem, and the first depthwise conv of stages 2, 3, 4 and 6) pad asymmetrically (Conv2dSame), and trunk BatchNorm eps = 1e-3. Parameter count, ONNX size (+ a few Pad nodes), read levels, MixStyle, cosine head, committee, decode, losses, augmentation, schedule, weight averaging and BN recalibration are all unchanged from experiment 20.
expected_outcome: Same as pre-registered for experiment 24: mission_score 0.0777 -> ~0.055-0.065 (best guess 0.06), mostly from abstentions turning into usable fixes: usable_fix_rate 93.0% -> ~94.5-95.5%, abstain 6.25% -> ~4-5%, false_fix_rate roughly flat at 0.5-1.0% (2-4 of 400 frames). Training-capture diagnostics should stay ~100% usable. Refutation: mission >= 0.0777 with usable <= 93% means the pretraining source of a fixed architecture is not what limits cross-survey transfer here. A far worse result (usable < 85%) would first be checked for a porting fault: padding asymmetry or an eps mismatch.
eli5: The drone's 'eyes' are a pair of image-recognition networks that learn from a large collection of everyday photos before they learn Berlin. Each time we gave them better early training, they got much better at recognising Berlin in a photograph they had never seen. The chip has no room for bigger eyes, so we keep exactly the same eyes but swap in a version first trained on 300 million photos, many of them deliberately blurred, noisy or with altered colours. We already tried this once, but the cloud computer never started, so the idea was never actually tested.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: NEW: same shape, different upbringing. The 128 px frame is enlarged to 224 px and read by two independent copies of EfficientNet-B0. Both copies now start from the Noisy Student weights (trained on ImageNet plus 300 million extra photographs under deliberate blur, noise and colour distortion; Apache-2.0) instead of plain ImageNet weights, with the TensorFlow-style padding those weights were trained with. Fine-tuned on Berlin at a tenth of the learning rate, each copy reads a 112-channel 14×14 map and a 320-channel 7×7 map. Each map is lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame, giving a 112-number place description; the flown weights are the average over the second half of training

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each); the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: unchanged from experiment 20: cross-survey style mixing inside the feature extractor (training only), angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate, 8 epochs, weight averaging over the second half with normalisation statistics re-measured

implementation_brief:
This is a RE-RUN of experiment 24, whose implementation was finished and never trained (AWS had no capacity). Do not re-design anything; restore that implementation exactly.

STEP 1 — restore the code. Copy runs/20261102_104104_experiment24/model_src/model.py -> model/model.py and runs/20261102_104104_experiment24/model_src/train.py -> model/train.py. First diff each against the current model/model.py and model/train.py (the experiment-20 champion). The ONLY differences allowed are experiment 24's: PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH -> model/pretrained/effb0ns_features7.pt, the TRUNK_WEIGHTS constant, the Conv2dSame class and its installation on the five stride-2 convs (stem features[0][0]; the depthwise conv features[i][0].block[1][0] for i in 2,3,4,6) in build_pretrained_trunk(), BatchNorm eps = 1e-3 on the trunk, and the docstring/log strings. If the diff shows any other change, revert that hunk to the champion's code.

STEP 2 — weights file. model/pretrained/effb0ns_features7.pt (14.65 MB) and model/pretrained/port_effb0_ns.py already exist (untracked) from experiment 24. Do NOT re-download if the file loads. Verify: (a) torch.load it, check that its keys are prefixed 'features.' and exactly match the key set and shapes of the champion's effb0_features7.pt; (b) build_pretrained_trunk() loads it with strict=True and the two shape asserts pass; (c) the tensors are NOT identical to effb0_features7.pt (sanity check that this is not the ImageNet file under a new name: e.g. features.0.0.weight must differ). If any check fails, re-run `.venv/bin/python -m model.pretrained.port_effb0_ns` (its numeric check vs a reference forward must pass at tol 1e-4) and STOP with a clear error if it cannot. Never fall back to IMAGENET1K_V1, because the experiment would then silently re-run the champion. Leave effb0_features7.pt untouched. Both files must stay under model/pretrained/ so the remote trainer's rsync of model/ ships them.

STEP 3 — strings. In train.py, update the record text that mentions experiment 24 so it reads 'experiment 25 (re-run of 24, which never trained: no AWS capacity)': the docstring note and train_info 'init'/'trunk_weights'. Change no logic beyond step 1.

SANITY before finishing: (1) build_model plus one forward/backward on a random batch on CPU: the loss is finite; (2) export_onnx on a freshly built model, then check with onnxruntime that a 1x3x128x128 input returns shape [1,3] with conf in [0,1], and that the file stays under 32 MiB (33,554,432 bytes) and is within a few KB of the champion's 31.69 MB; (3) host latency ~50 ms (gate 250 ms).

FIXED CONTRACTS (the frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI unchanged: `python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <d> [--data-dir] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]`, writes <out>/models/<area>.onnx and appends to <out>/train_info.json. ONNX contract (model/model.py docstring): input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] -> output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]], with u,v normalised map coords in [0,1] and conf in [0,1]; the whole decode stays inside the graph. Training reads ONLY buckets(meta, 'train'); nothing under model/ may open the truedop_2024 eval capture in any form. Nothing is downloaded at train or inference time. Do not edit any /FROZEN file.
